modern: Do not disturb yourself by thinking of the whole of your life. Do not let your thoughts take in all at once the various troubles which you may expect to come upon you: but on every occasion ask yourself, What is there in this which is unbearable and past enduring? For you will be ashamed to admit it. Next, remember that neither the future nor the past pains you, but only the present. And this is reduced to a very little, if only you set limits to it, and scold your mind if it is unable to hold out against even this.
original: Do not disturb thyself by thinking of the whole of thy life. Let not thy thoughts at once embrace all the various troubles which thou mayest expect to befall thee: but on every occasion ask thyself, What is there in this which is intolerable and past bearing? for thou wilt be ashamed to confess. In the next place remember that neither the future nor the past pains thee, but only the present. But this is reduced to a very little, if thou only circumscribest it, and chidest thy mind if it is unable to hold out against even this.
